narration.text: [softly] December, eighteen twenty. Tennessee. They are burying John Bell. [long pause] Witnesses said a voice laughed over the grave. And sang. Until the last mourner left. [long pause] The morning he died, the family found a small vial no one recognised. [long pause] [whispers] The voice said it had given him a dose. [long pause] [softly] For three years, it had talked. Visitors said it repeated sermons, word for word. [long pause] It pulled the covers off the children's beds. Every night. [long pause] It began in eighteen seventeen. With scratching. On the outside of the walls. [long pause] Almost all of this comes from one book, written seventy years later. The family's own account has never been found. [long pause] [whispers] This is the first night. You know how it ends.

prompts.laugh: A disembodied woman's laugh, distant and echoing across a frozen open field at dusk, cold wind, no music
prompts.gust: A sudden violent gust of winter wind sweeping across an open field, lantern flames sputtering out, snow hissing, then near silence
prompts.scratch: Slow claw-like scratching dragged along the outside of a rough wooden log cabin wall at night, heard from inside, crickets faint, no music
prompts.quilt: A heavy quilt slowly sliding off a bed and then yanked across old wooden floorboards in a quiet room, cloth rustle and drag, no music
